newsitem.title: UK: UK MacCulloch oilfield start delayed to end-May.
newsitem.headline: UK MacCulloch oilfield start delayed to end-May.

text.p: Conoco said on Monday first oil from its North Sea MacCulloch field had been delayed by a further couple of weeks and now was expected by around the end of May.

The start of production, originally due in December 1996, had been put back by some bad North Sea weather which had hampered commissioning of floating production vessel North Sea Producer, a company spokeswoman said.
MacCulloch, which has estimated recoverable reserves of 58 million barrels of crude oil similar to North Sea benchmark Brent, should see peak production hit 50-60,000 barrels per day (bpd).
Operator Conoco holds a 60 percent interest in MacCulloch. LASMO North Sea Plc owns the remaining 40 percent.

Oil from MacCulloch will be transported to Britain's Flotta terminal in the Orkney Islands but the North Sea Producer will also be equipped to load shuttle tankers if pipeline capacity to Flotta is not available.
One Flotta cargo was cancelled last week from the May loading programme as a a result of the MacCulloch delay.
Surplus gas will be exported via the Frigg pipeline system to St. Fergus.
